Hey velokartētāji, ko domājat par šo piezīmi?
https://www.openstreetmap.org/note/4986400

Note: 4986400
OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.
This topic was moved here from #general > Elizabetes ielas velo by HellMap.

Es uz to paskatījos, jā. Autors arī nomainīja vienu. Nu jā, mums ir kā ir. Vieni vispirms iekartē atsevišķi, otri pēc tam kā ceļa tegus vai arī otrādi. "Pareizi" jau gan neatdalītas velojoslas nav kartēt atsevišķi. Bet arguments parasti, lai varētu vismaz kaut kādu veloinfrastruktūru "redzēt". Jau daudz reižu ar dažādiem autoriem vai nu vienā vai otrā virzienā mainīts. Ja kāds no OSM lielākas kopienas pievērstu uzmanību, tad gan jau visi tie atsevišķie ātri tiktu nonesti. Bet pagaidām mēs ne par ko vietēji neesam vienojušies vēl...
Te pa kanāliem daudz piemēru. Changeset komentārus man slikums sameklēt visus.

Es veloinfrastruktūrā mazāk esmu iedziļinājies, varbūt vērts kaut kādu lokālo praksi definēt.
Atsevišķi kartētu grūtāk uzturēt.
Savukārt neatdalītu laikam specializētie velo rendereri arī rāda normāli, vai ne?

No pieredzes, atsevišķi kartētu noteikti vieglāk uzturēt, jo birkas un trajektorijas utt. nemaisās. Ceļi bieži saskaldīti katrā pagriezienā ar turn restricitoniem, dažādām sidewalk/parking birkām, utt. Piemēram Čaka ir 100 gabali un uz karta ir tas cycleway. Ja kaut kas jāmaina, tad visi 100 gabali.
Neatdalītu specializētie renderē jā, bet tur ir diezgan liela putra arī, ja daudz ceļu. Saprast var, bet krustojumos kaut kādos protams neko saprast no trajektorijām nevar, jo datos tās vispār nav.

Tad gandrīz vai labāk atsevišķi kartēt joslas tomēr?
Nez, pie kā ir nonākuši valstīs, kur to joslu ir daudz vairāk.
Kamēr tie nebūs redzami default slāni, es zīmēšu atsevišķi

Cik zinu, visur kur kartētāju ir vismaz nedaudz vairāk, joslas nekad nav atsevišķi. Tas ir gan wiki aprakstīts, gan katreiz apspriešanās secināts. Lūk tagad kāds arī pamanījis, ka Latvijā sazīmēts citādi. Protams vajadzētu darīt vai nu vienā veidā vai otrā, bet ne kā pie mums - kur pagadās tā, kur ne tā. Un vismaz cycleway=lane tegiem tām atsevišķām joslām jābūt saliktiem.
Es šajā tēmā īsti neesmu iedziļinājies - varbūt tiem, kuri vairāk sapratuši, ir iespēja dokumentēt kopienas lēmumu? Tad arī varētu vērt to piezīmi ciet (ar vai bez izmaiņām datos).
Tur jau tā lieta - kas tieši ir kopienas lēmums? Mums kaut kur 50 uz 50 viedokļi, cik es zinu.

Sarežģīti :)
Vai jaunais vektoru slānis situāciju kaut kā uzlabo vai nē?

I would like to have a go at this.

I think only following streets need correction:

  • Zirņu (some places)
  • Vesetas (some places)
  • Dzelzavas - Vaidavas - Ieriķu triangle
  • Bruniņieku (along) + Sporta (maybe)
  • Elizabetes
  • Dzirnavu
  • Vilhema Purvīša (northern segment)
  • Kalna/Ludzas and rest of the way to Akropole

My criteria: presence of plastic bollards / plastic bollards + rubber bricks / rubber bricks + streetside parking = separate cycleway. I think it's not controversial.
I have some doubts in two things:

  1. Only rubber bricks, with no parking or bollards, like it's on Sporta iela. I personally wouldn't consider it a protected infra, but open to arguments.
  2. Tagging different directions of same street differently. For example, "correct" tagging of Bruniņieku will result in only one side being rendered on default layer, which might cause confusion and erroneous edits/notes.

Please share your thoughts!

I have personally avoided doing this. But it is technically correct to not map physically-unseparated lanes as separate ways. One thing though - I would consider those rubber "bricks" as sufficient physical separation to count as separate, because it's not just paint that doesn't physically prevent crossing - bricks do. (May be not in cases where it's a very short section tho.) And yeah, different criteria can apply to opposite lanes and one can be separate and other not like Bruņinieku -- it can be a mess. But yeah, it sucks because none of it is in the default OSM layer and in most others that aren't dedicated to cycling.

I have thought about it some more, and I still thing it's correct to proceed with retagging.
I really dislike that most renderers don't show lanes.
But I can find some peace in "if they don't know better - only safe cycleways will be shown, but if they do - cycleOSM or OpenCycleMap are not hard to find"

I intend to proceed with the change this week.
I will not touch Sporta iela with its rubber bricks.

It's one of the 301. with "Iznemot :bike:", so opposite direction is open only to [trolley]buses and bicycles.

301. Iebraukt aizliegts

On Vaidavas (going South) technically, it's not a cycle lane at all. There is no bicycle road pictogram, so nothing legally makes it a cycle lane. It's just a road where vehicles are not allowed in this direction, except for bicycles (explicitly) and buses (implicitly). Which was already tagged like that. It's the same as Avotu https://www.mapillary.com/app/?pKey=640704295804679&focus=photo. I don't believe there are any places in Latvia with actual "share busway" signage as in a pictogram on the road, but I might not be aware of some location. As far as I know, it's either sharrows or no additional lane signage for bicycles.

Mapillary
Street-level imagery, powered by collaboration and computer vision.

Yes, I know that and familiar with this place.
But since in that southbound direction only one lane exists, and this lane only allows bicycles and buses, doesn't it make it share_busway?
Walks like a duck, etc, etc =)

Well, it doesn't. (Putting aside the fact that this is not a bus lane, so it could not by definition be a share_busway.) share_busway implies there is a dedicated lane consideration for bicycles. But this is just a lane like on every other road, just with access restrictions (in this direction). It might quack similar to a duck, but you know, if the whole premise is to tag accurately...
You convinced me: I removed share_busway on Vaidavas

Wow, just wow.
Both cycle lanes from Ludzas till Akropole and from Akropole till Kalna are a single path each.
Why wasn't EV10 going through segments like this? =)
It's crazy how I bike everywhere but have no idea what the street names are. Like, I have no idea what segment you mean :face_with_peeking_eye:
But yeah I guess you mean this. As far as I recall it wasn't seperated anywhere along N-S. Only on Ludzas in places
A lot of EV10 was mapped before these existed and no one has updated it since. If you start looking at cycle routes in Latvia, you'll find half or more of them are broken let alone outdated.

Well, if I wasn't editing those street right now, their names wouldn't mean much to me either =)
On Ludzas separation is not a "proper" separation but rather just traffic calmings near the intersections/crossings.
I mapped everything as lanes.
And re EV10: it doesn't go nowhere near these streets. What I meant is that both and new routes go through a bunch of tine segments which were a pain to click through even in the tool I used. If I could just unselect and then select new segments that were continuous runs of cycleway for 3-somthing kilometres, updating ev10 would go significantly faster and easier.

Ludzas is something I definitely wouldn't map as lanes. Because then stuff like https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1252489991 doesn't make sense anymore. You then need to split off the cycleway at each of these if not keeping it for the rest of the road.

OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.

markalex said:

select new segments that were continuous runs of cycleway for 3-somthing kilometres, updating ev10 would go significantly faster and easier

Yeah, that's one of the reasons I want to write my own route editor, so it can support pathfinding - you click a logical continuation segment and it paths to it through expected/logical route. This "click 500 segments" workflow is unusable. Every time I edited in Relatify I was wishing I could do this instead of zooming in into yet another 30 cm segment because of some random driveways

markalex said:

On Ludzas separation is not a "proper" separation but rather just traffic calmings

I don't think it should be, but if you are going to map them on road, then you need to map traffic calmings and buffers as well with cycle lane tags and delete the duplicate separately-mapped elements.

I don't think it should be, but if you are going to map them on road, then you need to map traffic calmings and buffers as well with cycle lane tags and delete the duplicate separately-mapped elements.

Dzirnavu was a hell to retag - for some completely mysterious to me reason segments there don't all go in the same direction.
I hope I caught change of direction every time, but will need to check it, once cycling tiles will be updated.
I think traffic_calming=choker+bicycle_bypass=yes might work for Ludzas.

That is for the road (node or segment) only. Cycle lane needs cycleway:separation=*, cycleway:buffer=* . choker does not apply to cycle lanes here because there is no physical change in lanes, although I have no idea how you can specify this now.
Also now all marked blue cycleway crossing are gone and I am not sure where you can readd this information now.
I guess at this point it's all the same problems with sidewalks mapped as road tags, but oh well. Hopefully, in the future OSM will shift to using separate ways like sidewalks did.

HellMap said:

That is for the road (node or segment) only. Cycle lane needs cycleway:separation=*, cycleway:buffer=* . choker does not apply to cycle lanes here because there is no physical change in lanes, although I have no idea how you can specify this now.

But it is a choker (maybe combination of choker and blister).
It narrows down whole width of the road to a lane of approximately car's width in middle + cycle lane.
Exactly, "+ cycle lane". So it is both. Previously bollards were mapped at the right distance from cycle lane as buffer, but now it needs to be on the road tags.
This is why I don't merge this stuff to roads where stuff like bollards exist, because it's annoying to map and maintain and just make the road split into multiple segments.

HellMap said:

Exactly, "+ cycle lane". So it is both. Previously bollards were mapped at the right distance from cycle lane as buffer, but now it needs to be on the road tags.

Yes, and chocker is put onto road. It indicates that some limitations are applied to a road, while bicycle_bypass=yesindicates that cycle lane is not affected.
Yes... Are we disagreeing about something?

I thought so.
I thought that this
HellMap said:

That is for the road (node or segment) only. Cycle lane needs cycleway:separation=*, cycleway:buffer=* . choker does not apply to cycle lanes here because there is no physical change in lanes, although I have no idea how you can specify this now.

means that you think that chocker is not enough.
And I think that it's enough: bollards, in this specific case, are not a "feature" of cycle lane, but rather of the choker. Whereas cycle lane just goes past it.
It is a feature of both. In this case the choker just matches the extents of separation. But nothing is stopping the choker from being longer or bollards from being further.

By the way, where are there actually chokers on Ludzas. I feel like we're discussing a hypothetical at the moment, since I can't think of a location that has this exact case. Even on Ludzas where traffic island splits the crossings, it doesn't choke them.

I finished with all streets that I considered for retagging, except for Vesetas.

I don't like situation on Vesetas: sides where lane is protected and not switching back and forth. Applying same principal as everywhere else (leaving protected lanes as separate way, folding unprotected into road) before would result in a hot mess, IMO.
Other options:

  1. fold everything into road, just use cycleway=lane vs cycleway=track as needed. None would be rendered on default layer.
  2. do nothing

I'd appreciate your input.
